speaker: Doctor
text:
Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are pregnant and experiencing vaginal bleeding with abdominal pain; how many weeks pregnant are you, and is this bleeding heavy or light?

REQUEST TEST: Serum beta-hCG
REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC)

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Hemoglobin: 10.2 g/dL (decreased), Platelets: 200,000 /μL, PT: 11 seconds, aPTT: 30 seconds. Ultrasound Abdomen and Pelvis: Findings suggestive of a disruption in the uterine wall continuity adjacent to the scar from the previous cesarean section, with associated hemoperitoneum.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is a medical emergency; the ultrasound findings of disruption near your previous C-section scar and hemoperitoneum are highly concerning for a uterine rupture. Please remain exactly where you are lying down and do not attempt to stand or walk until we can secure surgical intervention. Are you currently experiencing severe back pain, shoulder tip pain, or a sudden loss of fetal movement?

speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old woman, gravida 2, para 1, at 38 weeks' gestation. The patient reports experiencing vaginal bleeding for the past hour accompanied by severe abdominal pain. She mentions that she felt contractions before the onset of the bleeding, but the contractions ceased once the bleeding began. Her first childbirth was a cesarean section due to nonreassuring fetal heart rate.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Uterine Rupture at previous Cesarean Scar Site.

The ultrasound confirming disruption of the uterine wall continuity with hemoperitoneum, combined with your history of a prior C-section, cessation of contractions, and vaginal bleeding, is diagnostic for this life-threatening emergency. We are proceeding immediately to the operating room for exploratory laparotomy and hysterectomy.
